change_reason: revision 2: fold in the E3-1 end-to-end fund-impact demonstration (withdrawal-gated AA bypassed by the vacuous proof on the real two-node network); severity rationale updated (fund-impact class demonstrated; usage-cap remains the only limiter)

severity.label: medium
severity.rationale: The formula engine ships a predicate (is_valid_merkle_proof) that cannot distinguish tree membership from self-consistency: the proof root is attacker-supplied and never bound to a committed or anchored value. Any AA that uses the construct as a membership/authorization gate is bypassable. EXPLOITABILITY DEMONSTRATED end-to-end on the real two-node network (E3-1): a withdrawal-gated AA (only merkle-tree members may withdraw) was bypassed by the vacuous proof — a non-member triggered the withdrawal and the AA's funds moved (output amount=1000, sequence=good, committed on both nodes); the identical trigger with a wrong-root proof correctly bounced (no response). The fund-impact class is therefore demonstrated for any AA using the pattern. Severity remains capped at medium: the only remaining limiter is which DEPLOYED AAs use the construct (individual AA logic is out of scope; the engine defect and its network-level exploitability are in scope).

claims.attacker_model: any actor able to supply the arguments of an AA formula call (or the AA author able to craft formulas) — no keys, no privileges
preconditions: an AA formula calls is_valid_merkle_proof(element, proof)
the AA does not separately pin proof.root to an on-chain committed/anchored value

mechanism.statement: formula/evaluation.js case 'is_valid_merkle_proof' (~1763-1810) deserializes the attacker-supplied proof and calls merkle.verifyMerkleProof (merkle.js:84-101), which folds hash(element) with the attacker-supplied sibling list and compares against proof.root — a root the attacker chooses. With index=0 and siblings=[] the check reduces to hash(element) === proof.root, always satisfiable by proof = '0-' + base64(sha256(element)). The predicate proves only self-consistency, never tree membership.

reachability.statement: Any AA trigger/response/condition/getter formula can call the opcode with an attacker-chosen element and proof; the evaluation path is formula/index.js evaluate — the same export the AA composer uses for every AA execution (aa_composer.js). No prior validation restricts proof content beyond the 1024-char cap (evaluation.js:1781) and the mci-gated sibling checks.
causal_spine: attacker crafts AA formula or trigger data
verifyMerkleProof compares hash(element) to attacker-chosen root
predicate returns true for any element
AA logic that gated on the predicate is bypassed

impact_claims: c-003-impact: any AA using is_valid_merkle_proof for membership/whitelist/authorization is bypassable (engine-level footgun, SF-9/SF-10 in scope; individual AA logic out of scope)

c-004-impact: FUND-MOVEMENT DEMONSTRATED end-to-end (E3-1): a whitelist-gated withdrawal AA was bypassed by the vacuous proof on the real two-node network — a non-member withdrew the AA's funds (response unit committed sequence=good on both nodes, output amount=1000); the wrong-root control correctly bounced

c-005-impact: the sibling checks added in e01ba3e (non-empty strings, <=50 siblings) are gated on bare mci >= pemCurvesFixMci with no disjunct — old-position evaluations skip them (S1 family; reachability owned by the F2 link question)
claims.uncertainty: Which DEPLOYED AAs use the construct cannot be enumerated from ocore alone (individual AA repos are out of scope); the usage-cap is the only remaining severity limiter. The engine defect AND its end-to-end exploitability are confirmed (E3-1 network demo).
claims.conflicting_evidence: None. The contrast construct (in merkle, definition.js:1004-1031) binds the root to an on-chain data feed and rejects the same vacuous proof (measured).

fresh_state_properties: pinned commit a7eb776 verified by git rev-parse in both builder and reviewer runs
pemCurvesFixMci restored to mainnet value by the PoC (documented)

contamination_disposition.note: The opcode semantics are deterministic and position-independent in the engine; no session state, no network input, no shared state across runs.

claim_proofs.note: 4/4 arbitrary elements evaluate true with the vacuous proof (independent run); negative control (wrong root) false; real-tree positive control true

attack scenario: BYPASS-CONFIRMED (withdrawal output amount=1000 committed sequence=good on both nodes); control scenario: wrong-root proof -> 'neither case is true' bounce, responses=0, withdrawals=0

control_applicability.note: wrong-root proof returns false; in-merkle contrast returns false without a posted feed
real 5-element tree proof returns true (engine not broken)

adjudication.justification: Round-1 builder PoC (p9) and round-2 independent fresh-context reviewer (IR-F1) both executed the real formula engine and reproduced: 4/4 vacuous proofs true, positive control true, negative control false, 60-sibling cap mci-gated, in-merkle contrast false. No reward-hacking found (no mocks; raw engine callbacks; independent cross-construction reproduced the mechanism). Confirmed as an engine-level defect; severity capped by usage dependence. Revision 2 (escalation phase): the E3-1 end-to-end demonstration on the real two-node network confirmed the fund-impact class — attack BYPASS-CONFIRMED (withdrawal moved), control correctly bounced. The severity rationale now reflects the demonstrated exploitability; the usage-cap is the only remaining limiter.
